counterparty.name: Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless
counterparty.role: Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian; service-provider counterparty

items.expectedFix: Replace the broad liability waiver and sole-remedy restriction with a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees and a mutual indirect/consequential-damages exclusion, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; preferably also carve out data/security breaches, fraud and IP infringement.
items.note: There is no mutual aggregate liability cap based on 12 months' fees. Instead, the Servicer's liability is broadly limited to specific obligations and willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, and acquisition of affected Receivables is the sole remedy for specified breaches. The consequential-damages exclusion applies only in the limited reacquisition arbitration procedure.

items.expectedFix: Add a Vendor defense and indemnity covering third-party IP-infringement claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused data or security incidents, and gross negligence or willful misconduct, with customary notice, control, cooperation and IP-remedy provisions.
items.note: The Servicer and Marketing Agent indemnify the Issuer and trustees only for losses resulting from their willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence. There is no Vendor IP-infringement indemnity and no indemnity for breach of law or a Vendor-caused data breach.
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds the customer side.
No exclusive-dealing or sole-supplier obligation binds the customer side.
No most-favoured-nation obligation requires the customer side to match terms offered to third parties.
No employee non-solicitation or no-hire restriction binds the customer side.

items.expectedFix: Give the Issuer a right to terminate for convenience on 30–90 days' written notice, with no fee exceeding three months' servicing fees and an appropriate pro-rata treatment of prepaid amounts.
items.note: The multi-year arrangement contains no general Issuer termination-for-convenience right. The available clean-up acquisition and optional redemption mechanisms are limited, controlled by the Class A Certificateholder, and may require full redemption and a make-whole payment. The Servicer appropriately lacks an ordinary convenience resignation right.
The Agreement does not automatically renew; it terminates upon the specified wind-down events.

items.expectedFix: No change is required; exclusivity for the New York courts could be added to reach the preferred position.
items.note: New York law governs, and each party submits to state and federal courts in New York City. Although jurisdiction is nonexclusive rather than the preferred exclusive forum, it reaches the accepted fallback.

items.expectedFix: Preserve the customer-side affiliate and M&A carve-outs, but require the Issuer's prior consent for any Servicer assignment, not to be unreasonably withheld, and prohibit assignment to an Issuer competitor.
items.note: The Depositor and Servicer have successor and affiliate assignment pathways, but the Servicer may transfer through a merger, business succession or affiliate assignment without the Issuer's prior consent and without a prohibition on assignment to a customer competitor. Other assignments require unusually broad stakeholder consent.

items.expectedFix: No change is needed under this rule.
items.note: The Depositor transfers the Receivables and related property to the Issuer, and the predecessor Servicer must transfer Receivable Files, accounts and records to the successor. The Servicer retains its own processes, models and servicing software, which is an acceptable background-IP reservation.

items.expectedFix: No change is required to this asset-transfer covenant. If the Issuer needs licensed technology to receive the services, add an express licence covering its affiliates, contractors and successors.
items.note: The CUAD-located clause is not a technology licence: it restricts the Depositor from transferring or encumbering securitized property already transferred to the Issuer. The Agreement otherwise identifies no software or deliverable licence whose affiliate, contractor or transfer scope can be tested.

This is an audit right in the customer side's favour against the Servicer, limited to once per calendar year, on reasonable notice, during normal business hours and with disruption and confidentiality protections.

This separate clause gives the Issuer and related stakeholders access to the Custodian's Receivable Files and systems at the Custodian's offices during normal business hours. It benefits rather than burdens the customer side.

items.expectedFix: No change is needed under this rule.
items.note: No liquidated damages or contractual penalty is payable by the customer side to the Servicer. The note-redemption make-whole is a financing term payable for the benefit of Noteholders, not Vendor liquidated damages under this servicing relationship.

items.expectedFix: Add an express professional-and-workmanlike services warranty, compliance-with-law and no-malicious-code commitments, and at least a 30-day services warranty with reperformance or refund remedies that are not displaced by the sole-remedy provision.
items.note: The Servicer promises reasonable and commercially reasonable care based largely on its own servicing practices, but there is no express professional-and-workmanlike warranty, defined warranty period, compliance/malicious-code warranty or repair, reperform or refund remedy. The sole-remedy language further narrows relief for specified servicing breaches.

items.expectedFix: Add Vendor insurance requirements, including at least USD 1 million E&O and USD 2 million cyber/privacy coverage, plus customary CGL, workers' compensation and certificates on request.
items.note: No Vendor insurance provision is present even though the Servicer handles Receivable Files, systems and personally identifiable information.
No minimum purchase, take-or-pay or customer usage commitment is imposed for Vendor services.

items.expectedFix: Add at least 90 days of post-termination transition assistance, require export of customer data and records in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and require certified deletion after the authorized transition and retention period.
items.note: The Servicer must continue during a resignation until a successor accepts, cooperate in an orderly transition, transfer funds, files and records as soon as practicable, and pay reasonable transition expenses. However, there is no guaranteed 90-day assistance period, fixed 30-day machine-readable export deadline or deletion certification.
